_meta.indication: Indicated to accelerate the time to upper and lower gastrointestinal recovery following partial large or small bowel resection surgery with primary anastomosis
_meta.receipt_date: August 10, 2007 (NDA dated August 9, 2007, constituting a complete response to the November 3, 2006 action letter)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter study (55 US centers), 1:1 randomization to alvimopan 12 mg bid or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Men and women at least 18 years of age undergoing partial small or large bowel resection with primary anastomosis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time (hours) to recovery of GI function after end of surgery, measured by the 2-component composite endpoint GI2 (maximum of time to first bowel movement and time to first solid food)
pivotal_trials.n: 654 randomized (329 alvimopan, 325 placebo); MITT 629 (317 alvimopan, 312 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint GI2 (recovery of GI function) hazard ratio 1.53 (95% CI 1.29, 1.82) for alvimopan 12 mg vs placebo, p<0.001

nct_ctgov.title: Study of Alvimopan for the Management of Opioid-induced Postoperative Bowel Dysfunction/Postoperative Ileus

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=3% and >=1% placebo) in bowel resection patients were anemia (5.2% vs 4.2% placebo), dyspepsia (7.0% vs 4.6%), hypokalemia (9.5% vs 8.5%), back pain (3.3% vs 1.7%), and urinary retention (3.2% vs 2.1%). Most serious safety signal: a higher number of myocardial infarctions reported with alvimopan 0.5 mg twice daily vs placebo in a 12-month chronic-pain study.
target_moa: Alvimopan is a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor (PAM-OR) antagonist; a selective antagonist of the human mu-opioid receptor (Ki 0.4 nM) that antagonizes the peripheral effects of opioids on GI motility and secretion without reversing central analgesic effects

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: FOR SHORT-TERM HOSPITAL USE ONLY. ENTEREG is available only for short-term (15 doses) use in hospitalized patients; only hospitals registered in and meeting all requirements of the ENTEREG Access Support and Education (E.A.S.E.) program may use ENTEREG.

rems.type: A REMS is required to ensure the benefits outweigh the risk of myocardial infarction; it consists of a communication plan, elements to assure safe use (the E.A.S.E. program restricting use to registered hospitals), an implementation system, a timetable for assessments, and assessments of the REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: FDA's Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee met January 23, 2008; the committee recommended approval by a 9 to 6 vote with a tighter risk management plan

description.text: Revised the Indication and Usage section (relabeling to a revised indication)

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the Indication and Usage, Warnings and Precautions and Clinical Studies sections of the package insert and proposed modifications to the approved risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS).

summary.text: The alvimopan development program for postoperative ileus received fast track status in February 2004; the application was submitted under the Pilot 1 Continuous Marketing Application program, had Standard review priority, and was approved in its third review cycle (after two prior approvable letters) with a REMS including the E.A.S.E. program and a boxed warning for short-term hospital use only.

This is the third review cycle for Entereg, this approval follows allowable actions taken for the previous 2 submissions.

In accordance with 505-1 of the FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Entereg (alvimopan) Capsules, 12 mg, to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of myocardial infarction.

requirement.text: Conduct a study of Entereg for acceleration of gastrointestinal recovery in pediatric patients age greater than 1 month up to 16 years undergoing bowel resection surgery (deferred pediatric study under PREA/505B(a)).

citations.quote: - Conduct a study of Entereg for the acceleration of gastrointestinal recovery in pediatric patients age greater than 1 month up to 16 years undergoing bowel resection surgery. The study will measure the time to first tolerated feed, population pharmacokinetic parameters, the proportion of postoperative days with stool passed while in hospital, length of hospital stay, the need for postoperative nasogastric tube insertion for symptoms of postoperative ileus, and safety.

requirement.text: Conduct a study of Entereg for acceleration of gastrointestinal recovery in pediatric patients age 0 to 1 month undergoing bowel resection surgery (deferred pediatric study under PREA/505B(a)).

citations.quote: - Conduct a study of Entereg for the acceleration of gastrointestinal recovery in pediatric patients age 0 to 1 month undergoing bowel resection surgery. The study will measure population pharmacokinetic parameters, safety, and time to first tolerated feed while in the hospital.

requirement.text: Required under 505(o): a multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group clinical trial of Entereg for the management of postoperative ileus in patients undergoing radical cystectomy, to assess the signal of serious risk of myocardial infarction.
